description: Declared with `only`. — this silently disables every other test in the file, so the suite goes green while almost nothing ran
`return` inside the clause that runs on the way out — it replaces whatever the block was leaving with, so a failure raised in the body disappears and nothing anywhere records that it happened
Calls itself 1 times per invocation with no memo in sight. — there is nothing that can stop it, so the first call takes the stack down with it
`rows` is changed while it is being walked. — the walk and the change disagree about what is left, so elements are skipped or seen twice depending on where the change landed
`case 1:` runs on into the arm below — the arm below runs too, and nothing written here says whether that was wanted or forgotten
`(kind === "a")` is asked twice in one chain — the second arm cannot be reached, so whatever it was written to do has never run and nobody has noticed
Both arms of this branch do the same thing. — the decision changes nothing, so either it is not a decision or one arm was meant to differ and does not
`count` is compared against itself. — the answer is decided before it runs, so either the comparison does nothing or one side was meant to be something else
`found = a + b` assigns where a condition is expected. — it reads as a comparison and behaves as a write, which is why it is the typo that survives review
This catch clause has an empty body. — the failure is swallowed silently, so the first sign of it is wrong data somewhere far away with nothing in the logs to connect the two
This statement cannot run: the block always returns before reaching it. — this code cannot run, so whatever it was meant to do is not happening and has not been happening
`loadOne` answers later and nothing takes the answer. — nothing waits for it and nothing hears if it fails, so the failure arrives somewhere with no idea what asked for it
`expect(add(1, 1)).toBe(add(1, 1));` has the same expression on both sides — it holds the code to whatever the code already does, so it passes through every change including the one that breaks it
`RegExp` runs on every pass of the loop. — the same pattern is parsed and compiled on every pass when once would do, and compiling is the expensive half of matching
Declared with `skip`. — a skipped test is a question nobody answered; it reports green forever while the behaviour it named goes unchecked
Parameter `total` is reassigned inside the function. — the caller's value changes without the call site saying so, which is the hardest kind of change to find when it turns out to be wrong
Parameter `value` is reassigned inside the function. — the caller's value changes without the call site saying so, which is the hardest kind of change to find when it turns out to be wrong
